guide.title: Before you pay
guide.text: Ask for the registration document, the Certificate of Conformity (COC) and the service history. Check that the VIN on the car matches the papers, and that CO₂ and the emission class match what you entered here.

guide.title: Paperwork
guide.text: Get a signed purchase contract or invoice, both parts of the registration document (in Germany: Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I and II) and the COC.

guide.title: Getting it home
guide.text: Drive it on export plates with insurance (in Germany: Ausfuhrkennzeichen from the local registration office), or have it transported.

guide.title: Conformity check
guide.text: At an authorised technical service in Slovenia, have the car's conformity checked (ugotavljanje skladnosti). The COC makes this quicker.

guide.title: Motor vehicle tax
guide.text: Declare and pay DMV to FURS (in eDavki or at a tax office) before you register the car.

guide.title: Registration
guide.text: Take out insurance, then have the technical inspection and register the car at a registration organisation.

guideVat.title: VAT
guideVat.text: Report the purchase to FURS and pay 22 % Slovenian VAT. Pay the seller the price without their VAT.

about.title: How Cargregator works
about.p1: You set your filters once. For each site, Cargregator builds a link to that site's own search page with your filters applied. When you press Open, the site's results open in a new tab.
about.p2: We don't copy, store or show any listings. Everything you see after pressing Open is on the original site.
about.p3: Not every site supports every filter. Each card tells you which filters it couldn't apply, so you can set them on the site.
about.privacy: No accounts and no cookies. Your last search and saved searches stay in this browser. Your location is only used to find the nearest city and is never sent anywhere.
about.beta: The sites change their links from time to time. If a link opens the wrong results, please let us know.

carInfo.title: Know the car before you buy
carInfo.intro: Pick a make and model to get a feel for the car: road tests, crash-test ratings, reliability data and recalls, by generation.
carInfo.unreviewed: Generations and engines are AI-assisted from EU registration data and not yet reviewed. Recalls come from EU Safety Gate and are matched to a generation by model and production years, so always check a car's VIN with the manufacturer.
carInfo.reportPlaceholder: What is wrong or missing on this page?
carInfo.reportThanks: Thanks, we will look into it.
carInfo.reportFailed: Could not send the report. Please try again later.
carInfo.vinNote: EU notices name models and years, not individual cars: check the VIN with the manufacturer.
carInfo.genRecalls: Recalls for this generation. EU notices rarely name the engine, so check which versions are affected.
carInfo.soonEngine: The full report for this engine (known failures, running costs, what to check before buying) is coming soon.
carInfo.soon: Full report with failures and costs coming soon.
carInfo.noModels: No models in the guide yet.
carInfo.linksIntro: Independent road tests, crash ratings and reliability data. Links open the source site.
carInfo.summarySoon: A summary, pros and cons, and the common problems of each generation are coming soon. Until then, the sources below are the best place to start.
carInfo.recallsIntro: Published on EU Safety Gate and matched to a generation by model and production years.
carInfo.failuresIntro: Recurring faults reported for this generation, most likely and most expensive first. Repair costs are rough estimates for an independent garage in Slovenia.
carInfo.annualCostHint: typical service and repairs, fuel excluded
carInfo.aiChecked: AI-assisted report; every problem was checked against its sources, but not yet reviewed by a person.
carInfo.genFailures: Problems that affect the whole generation
